metadata.title: Pólya's Recurrence Theorem: The Drunk Man and the Drunk Bird

canonical_sources.title: Über eine Aufgabe der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung betreffend die Irrfahrt im Straßennetz
Probability: Theory and Examples (random walk recurrence, Chapter 4)
Random Walks and Electric Networks
canonical_sources.authors: Peter G. Doyle, J. Laurie Snell

pedagogy.problem_statement: A walker takes unbiased, independent random steps on a lattice. Does it return to where it started, and does the answer depend on the number of dimensions?
pedagogy.core_thesis: For the simple symmetric random walk on the integer lattice Z^d, the walker returns to its start with probability 1 when d = 1 or 2 (recurrent) and with probability strictly less than 1 when d >= 3 (transient). The reason is that the chance of being at the origin at step 2n decays like n^(-d/2), and the expected number of returns is the sum of those chances.
pedagogy.mental_model: Space gives a wanderer room to avoid its past. On a plane, paths keep crossing themselves and the start; in three dimensions there is so much room that after a while the walker simply never crosses back.
pedagogy.key_takeaway: A drunk man will find his way home, but a drunk bird may get lost forever: the same random rule gives certain return in two dimensions and roughly a one-in-three chance of return in three.
verified_claims: The simple symmetric random walk on Z^d is recurrent for d = 1 and d = 2 and transient for d >= 3 (Polya, 1921).
In 2D the walker returns to the origin with probability 1 and, by recurrence, returns infinitely often with probability 1.
In 3D the probability of ever returning to the origin is about 0.3405373 (Polya's random walk constant p(3)), so the walker never returns with probability about 0.6595.
Return probabilities in higher dimensions: p(4) = 0.1932017, p(5) = 0.1351786, p(6) = 0.1047155 (computed from the Watson-type integral G(d) = integral of e^(-t) I0(t/d)^d dt, p = 1 - 1/G).
The probability of being at the origin at step 2n is u_2n ~ 1/(pi n) for d = 2 and u_2n ~ 2 (3/(4 pi n))^(3/2) for d = 3 (local limit theorem).
The walk is recurrent iff the sum over n of u_2n diverges (expected number of visits to the origin is infinite). Sum of 1/(pi n) diverges; sum of n^(-3/2) converges.
For d = 3 the expected number of returns is G(3) - 1 = p/(1-p) = 0.5164, where G(3) = 1.5163861.
In 1D and 2D the expected time of the first return to the origin is infinite even though return is certain (null recurrence).
The line 'A drunk man will find his way home, but a drunk bird may get lost forever' is attributed to Shizuo Kakutani (secondary attribution; present as 'is said to have put it').
anti_patterns: Do not say the bird is certain to be lost: it returns with probability about 0.34.
Do not say the man gets home quickly or within a bounded number of steps; the return is certain but the expected wait is infinite.
Do not present the model as a prediction about real birds or real drunk people; it is an idealised unbiased lattice walk.
Do not call the 3D return probability 1/3 exactly; it is 0.3405 (about one in three).
Do not imply 'transient' means the walker can never return; it means it returns only finitely many times with probability 1.
Do not draw a walk that is not a real simulation of the stated rule.

entities.name: Random walker position
entities.role: Position after n steps; starts at the origin (home).

entities.name: Dimension
entities.role: 2 for the man on a city grid, 3 for the bird.

entities.name: Step
entities.role: One of the 2d unit vectors chosen uniformly at random, independently each step.

entities.name: Return probability
entities.role: Probability the walk ever returns to the origin.

entities.name: Probability of being home at step 2n
entities.role: Terms whose sum decides recurrence (odd steps cannot be at the origin).

entities.name: Expected visits to the origin (including time 0)
entities.role: Finite iff transient; then G = 1/(1 - p).

equations.spoken_form: In two dimensions the chance of being home at step two n is about one over pi n
In three dimensions it is proportional to n to the minus three halves
The expected number of visits home is one over one minus the return probability
equations.context: Links the series to recurrence: G infinite iff p = 1.

equations.spoken_form: The three dimensional return probability is about point three four

algorithmic_steps.mathematical_operation: S_{k+1} = S_k + X_k with X_k uniform on the 2d unit vectors
algorithmic_steps.state_effect: Walker moves one lattice step in a random axis direction.

algorithmic_steps.mathematical_operation: R = number of n >= 1 with S_n = 0; E[R] = sum_{n>=1} u_2n
algorithmic_steps.state_effect: Expected number of returns equals the series of home-odds.

algorithmic_steps.mathematical_operation: sum 1/(pi n) = infinity (d=2); sum n^(-3/2) < infinity (d=3)
algorithmic_steps.state_effect: d=2: infinitely many returns, certain; d=3: finitely many, escape with probability 1 - p(3).

scene_blueprint.title: Hook
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Pose the contrast: two random walkers, one certain to get home, one maybe never.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Two panels, a 2D grid with a blue walker and a 3D lattice with an amber walker, trace short walks while two statements land.

scene_blueprint.title: The Man
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Show a real 2D walk drifting, looping and returning to the door; note the infinite expected wait.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: City-grid lattice, blue leading dot with trail, step counter, pulse ring at the door when step 286 lands home.

scene_blueprint.title: The Bird
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Show a real 3D walk flying away, then the roughly one-in-three return odds with a 12-bird simulation.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Isometric lattice, amber leading dot with ground shadow; zoom-out into 12 simulated birds drawn until first return or 3000 steps, green if they returned and red otherwise; tally and p = 0.3405.

scene_blueprint.title: The Theorem
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: State Polya's theorem: recurrent for d = 1, 2; transient for d >= 3, with the return probability falling with d.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Dimension table d = 1 to 5 with RECURRENT/TRANSIENT badges and return probabilities.

scene_blueprint.title: Why
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Explain the mechanism: home-odds decay like 1/n in 2D and n^(-3/2) in 3D; one sum diverges, the other converges.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Log-log plot of u_2n for d = 2 and 3, then running sum of expected returns on log x: blue keeps climbing, amber flattens at 0.516.

scene_blueprint.title: Close
scene_blueprint.pedagogical_objective: Land the takeaway with the Kakutani line, flagged as an attribution, and the idealisation caveat.
scene_blueprint.visual_action: Quote card with the two outcomes, d = 2: p = 1 and d = 3: p = 0.34, holding to the end.
